variants.title: Version 1 — Paired planes
variants.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup / architectural landing-page art direction. Produce ONE full-width desktop website landing-page composition, landscape 16:9, meticulously designed and rendered. This is a flat screenshot of the actual proposed website viewport, NOT a browser/device mockup, NOT a poster, NOT a triptych. The real webpage's large 3D construction assemblies ARE its text and product-media surfaces. Hierarchy: a restrained navigation strip across the top; a very large readable headline directly on a front-facing precast concrete assembly; smaller prose and an action on that same concrete; a separate substantial framed glazed facade assembly that carries the product-film area; clearly three-dimensional contoured terrain covering the lower third; one dramatic building shadow across the open background. Use the provided image 1 ONLY as visual reference for its MIDDLE 'SHADOW ASSEMBLY' panel: warm ochre ground/backdrop, mineral concrete, dark steel, long sharp architectural shadows. Do not repeat the three-panel board, fragments, titles, or its other concepts. Image 2 is the existing SiteWise programme interface, a supporting insert for the product-film surface. Use it as the dark media area's content, preserving its general blue-bar programme arrangement; treat as a demonstration still, don't invent dashboards or statistics.
Common visual world: warm sand and rich ochre cyclorama, ivory/grey precast, subtly green-edged clear low-iron glazing in a real slender dark aluminium frame, hard directional architectural lighting, warm shadows. Front-on camera with just enough downward angle to show the ground, minimal perspective convergence. The faces carrying type must be almost parallel to the image plane, with a slight visible side return proving their thickness. Concrete feels like an actual factory-made structural facade panel, substantial 180-220mm edge, small chamfers and 2 discreet realistic lifting recesses at its top EDGE; minimal pores, broad calm face for text. Glass feels like one full glazed facade module, with credible perimeter extrusion/gasket and visible transparent edge zones, no internal mullion across the film. NO tiny scattered construction fragments, pipes, floating beams or debris. Limit composition to TWO dominant architectural assemblies with optional ONE supporting concrete footing. These may hover slightly with a defined air gap.
Terrain MUST have real 3D relief: broad sculpted irregular topographic terraces with 5-8 clearly visible elevation steps and shaded vertical risers, smoothly curving contour edges, a shallow valley and a higher shoulder. Like a refined architectural terrain model at building scale. NOT flat ground with drawn contour lines, NOT a staircase, not a canyon or enormous cliffs, not concentric rings all centred on the panels. Terrain continues to viewport edges. Background leaves a substantial open shadow-receiving region: a legible cast shadow of a complete two-storey building with slab bands, columns and a stair outline, in the upper open backdrop behind the assemblies. This shadow suggests the moving cinematic reveal; it must remain clearly visible, not hidden by copy or media. Stylised deliberately choreographed shadow illusion; no physical building in the backdrop.
Typography: calm contemporary Satoshi-like sans serif, generous space, precise hierarchy, dark ink on pale concrete. Exact website text only: brand 'SiteWise' at top left; nav 'Open SiteWise' and 'Book a project walkthrough' at top right. Headline 'Read. Organise. Update.' large on concrete, with line breaks as composition requires. Supporting sentence 'The New AI Powered Construction Management Platform.' beneath it in restrained small text. One small button 'Book a project walkthrough' on the concrete. Small media caption 'Product walkthrough' outside the image insert. No concept title, no labels such as placeholder, no render annotations, no metrics, no new slogans, no fine-print claims. Keep the top nav on calm uninterrupted background; strong text contrast. Product film area is a dark, nearly frontal rectilinear 16:10 surface nested on the glazing, with enough uncovered glass perimeter to recognise it as a physical glazed assembly. No laptop, screen bezel, rounded software card, decorative glassmorphism, neon, gradients behind text or futuristic holograms. High-fidelity architectural 3D plus genuinely composed web typography. Preserve whitespace and reading order.

LAYOUT A — PAIRED UPRIGHT PLANES. Header occupies top 10% with generous left/right gutters. Main scene occupies remaining 90%. Left: one tall broad upright rectangular solid precast wall panel fills x=7-43%, y=20-82%, its entire front face available for the headline broken into three stacked lines 'Read.' / 'Organise.' / 'Update.', prose and button beneath. The concrete hangs just 100mm above its local terrace; its right-hand edge is thick and visible. Right: one larger LANDSCAPE glazed facade panel fills x=50-94%, y=39-80%, nearly square to the viewer with one narrow return, the dark programme-film image inset within it. Left and right are independent complete objects, balanced by a generous central gap, not joined into a building. One low full rectangular concrete pad footing can be embedded under the left panel if needed for grounding, no other elements. Terrain has most relief at bottom left and flows gently toward the lower right. Crucially, behind the two panels, x=43-88%, y=12-38%, keep a BIG recognisable complete-building cast shadow visible in the ochre background. Deep bright sidelight from upper left, long clean shadows. Copy and media each immediately readable. Warm, restrained, material, confident.

LAYOUT B — PRECAST PORTAL. Header across top 10%. ONE monumental upright full precast facade WALL assembly fills x=8-91%, y=22-80%, nearly front-on. It is a credible prefabricated concrete facade panel, not two separate slabs or a classical arch. The left solid face carries the three-line headline, supporting sentence and button with generous padding. The opening is landscape and has a deep convincing concrete reveal. A complete rectangular glazed facade module floats slightly IN FRONT OF and 4% to the RIGHT of this opening, so the window reveal is visible on its left and top; that glazing holds the dark programme-film insert, clearly in front of the window, almost face-on. The wall hovers over an irregular three-dimensional cut-and-fill site platform, broad curves and visible raised terraces in the lower third, with a couple of solid embedded support pads immediately below the wall but no scattered fragments. Background ochre field is visible all around and through the gap; a LARGE crisp complete-building shadow rises BEHIND and above the portal in the upper central and right background, y=10-29%, and continues down one unobscured side. Frame the whole viewport as architecture becoming the webpage itself. Modest perspective only: headline, opening and film must read squarely. Dramatic warm directional light, rich reveal shadows and thin glazed highlights, no excessive concrete texture over copy.

LAYOUT C — CONTOUR COURT, A WIDE STEPPED COMPOSITION. Header across top 10%. A LONG LOW UPRIGHT FULL PRECAST facade panel, broad width about twice its height, occupies x=6-67%, y=23-64%, floating slightly above the raised left terrace. This is a VERTICAL billboard-like architectural wall panel with true thick construction edges and recessed lifting sockets, NOT a horizontal tabletop or slab viewed from above. Its large front-facing face carries the headline in TWO lines 'Read. Organise.' / 'Update.' across its upper left; smaller supporting prose and a compact button occupy its lower LEFT, always fully unobscured. High legibility, elegant balanced density, no extra objects.
